title: Queue_free() prevents signal callback execution in Node scripts, but using a Callable wrapper works for Resource scripts
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.1stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.rc1 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12490F (12 threads) - 31.81 GiB memory

### Issue description

I've encountered an issue: If a node has a script with a method _on_time_out() that contains a print statement, and in _ready() the node creates a scene tree timer for 1 second, connects its timeout signal to _on_time_out(), and then calls queue_free(), neither using timeout.connect(_on_time_out) nor timeout.connect(func(): _on_time_out()) results in the print statement being executed.

Another scenario: A Resource script has the same method, and this resource is held by a node. After connecting the timer's timeout signal to the method in the resource script using the same two approaches, and then calling queue_free() on the node that holds the resource, timeout.connect(_on_time_out) does not work, but timeout.connect(func(): _on_time_out()) does execute the callback as expected.

Demo:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ec3fb69-e635-4030-be15-6413af92a220

### Steps to reproduce

Test the two approaches in the demonstration above and observe the results.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[callable_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26116092/callable_bug.zip)
